cues.text: How are you getting on with your art project, Tom?
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: OK. Like, they gave us the theme of birds to base our project on, and I'm not really all that interested in wildlife. But I'm starting to get into it. I've pretty well finished the introductory stage.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: So have I. When they gave us all those handouts with details of books and websites to look at, I was really put off, but the more I read, the more interested I got.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Me too. I found I could research so many different aspects of birds in art - colour, movement, texture. So I was looking forward to the Bird Park visit.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: What a letdown! It poured with rain and we hardly saw a single bird. Much less use than the trip to the Natural History Museum.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Yeah, I liked all the stuff about evolution there. The workshop sessions with Dr Fletcher were good too, especially the brainstorming sessions.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: I missed those because I was ill. I wish we could've seen the projects last year's students did.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Mm. I suppose they want us to do our own thing, not copy.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Have you drafted your proposal yet?
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Yes, but I haven't handed it in. I need to amend some parts. I've realised the notes from my research are almost all just descriptions, I haven't actually evaluated anything. So I'll have to fix that.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Oh, I didn't know we had to do that. I'll have to look at that too. Did you do a timeline for the project?
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Yes, and a mind map.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Yeah, so did I. I quite enjoyed that. But it was hard having to explain the basis for my decisions in my action plan.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: What?
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: You know, give a rationale.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: I didn't realise we had to do that. OK, I can add it now. And I've done the video diary presentation, and worked out what I want my outcome to be in the project.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Someone told me it's best not to be too precise about your actual outcome at this stage, so you have more scope to explore your ideas later on. So I'm going to go back to my proposal to make it a bit more vague.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Really? OK, I'll change that too then.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: One part of the project I'm unsure about is where we choose some paintings of birds and say what they mean to us. Like, I chose a painting of a falcon by Landseer. I like it because the bird's standing there with his head turned to one side, but he seems to be staring straight at you. But I can't just say it's a bit scary, can I?
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: You could talk about the possible danger suggested by the bird's look.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Oh, OK.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: There's a picture of a fish hawk by Audubon I like. It's swooping over the water with a fish in its talons, and with great black wings which take up most of the picture.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: So you could discuss it in relation to predators and food chains?
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Well actually I think I'll concentrate on the impression of rapid motion it gives.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Do you know that picture of a kingfisher by van Gogh - it's perching on a reed growing near a stream.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Yes it's got these beautiful blue and red and black shades.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Mm hm. I've actually chosen it because I saw a real kingfisher once when I was little. I was out walking with my grandfather, and I've never forgotten it.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: So we can use a personal link?
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Sure.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: OK. There's a portrait called William Wells, I can't remember the artist but it's a middle-aged man who's just shot a bird. And his expression, and the way he's holding the bird in his hand suggests he's not sure about what he's done. To me it's about how ambiguous people are in the way they exploit the natural world.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Interesting. There's Gauguin's picture Vairumati. He did it in Tahiti. It's a woman with a white bird behind her that is eating a lizard, and what I'm interested in is what idea this bird refers to. Apparently, it's a reference to the never-ending cycle of existence.
cues.speaker: JESS

cues.text: Wow. I chose a portrait of a little boy. Giovanni de Medici. He's holding a tiny bird in one fist. I like the way he's holding it carefully so he doesn't hurt it.
cues.speaker: TOM

cues.text: Ah right.
cues.speaker: JESS
